Retry a function without blocking

Source: R/async_retry.R
async_retry.Rd

Asynchronous version of retry(), for functions that return a promise. It uses the same strategies and hooks, but schedules the next attempt with later::later() instead of sleeping, so the session is free between attempts.

Usage

async_retry(
  f,
  stop = stop_never(),
  wait = wait_none(),
  retry = retry_all(),
  before_sleep = before_sleep_none(),
  after_sleep = after_sleep_none(),
  reraise = FALSE,
  retry_error_callback = NULL
)

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

stop

A stop condition, e.g. stop_after_attempt(). Defaults to never stopping.

wait

A wait strategy. Defaults to no waiting.

retry

A retry condition. Defaults to retrying every error.

before_sleep, after_sleep

Hooks run before and after each sleep, see before_sleep_log() and after_sleep_log().

reraise

If TRUE, re-throw the last error when stop fires instead of throwing a retry_error.

retry_error_callback

Optional function called with the final state when stop fires. Its return value is returned instead of throwing. The state is a list with attempt, wait, elapsed, error and value.

Value

A decorator. The decorated function returns a promise.

Details

The decorated function returns a promise. It resolves with the first acceptable result, and rejects with the last error, or a retry_error once stop fires. The wrapped function may return a promise or a plain value, and a rejection or a thrown error counts as a failure.

Use it as the outermost decorator. timeout() cannot bound a promise, so cap each attempt with async_timeout(). The hooks and retry_error_callback run in the event loop, so keep them quick. Needs the promises and later packages, and an event loop for the promise to settle.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
n <- 0
flaky <- function() {
  n <<- n + 1
  if (n < 3) stop("not yet")
  n
}
f := async_retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(5), wait = wait_fixed(0.05)) %@%
  flaky
promises::then(f(), function(value) cat("worked on attempt", value, "\n"))

# Shiny and plumber run the event loop for you. In a script, run it yourself.
while (!later::loop_empty()) later::run_now(0.1)
} # }
